This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of MV Act, praying to allow the above Misc. First Appeal and consequently be pleased to set aside the judgment and award dated 01.09.2018 passed by II Addl.

Senior Civil Judge & MACT Kalaburagi, in MVC No.293/2012 and consequently allow the claim petition filed by the appellants and further be pleased to grant compensation against the respondents jointly and severally.

This appeal having been heard through physical hearing/video conference and reserved for Judgment on 31.01.2023, coming on for pronouncement of Judgment this day, T.G. Shivashankare Gowda, J., delivered the following:
 MFA No.202636/2019  3  JUDGMENT

The petitioners are before this court challenging the judgment dated 01.09.2018 passed in M.V.C.No.293/2012 on the file of II Additional Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T., Kalaburagi, in dismissing the claim petition.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties will be referred with respect to their status before the Tribunal.

3. Briefly stated the facts are that, the first petitioner is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the minor son,
petitioner Nos.3 and 4 are the parents and petitioner No.5 is the younger brother of one Basawaraj Kesaratagi, the deceased.

On 17.06.2011 at about 11.00 a.m. on Jewargi-Sindagi Road near Nelogi Cross, the deceased along with his friend riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA-32/X-6605 from Telgabal to Gulbarga side, at that time, from the opposite direction, a Tata Sumo bearing Parwati And Ors vs Raj Ahmed Bhatliwale And Anr on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186652813/
2 registration No.KA- 32/M-2961 dashed against the motor cycle causing injuries to the deceased.
He died on the way to hospital.
The petitioners being the dependants of the deceased have claimed compensation of Rs.19,45,000/- before the Tribunal.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company, denying the very accident.
The parties have led the evidence.

The Tribunal came to the conclusion that the accident was not proved and relied on the judgment of this Court in M.F.A.No.200493/2014 (MV) DD 10.11.2016 arising out of the same accident and dismissed the claim petition.

Aggrieved by the order of dismissal, the petitioners are before this Court, urging that though positive evidence was placed before the Tribunal establishing the alleged accident, it was not considered, the Tribunal was erred in relying on the judgment of this court in M.F.A.No.200493/2014 in dismissing the claim petition and sought for assessment of the compensation.

4. We have heard the arguments of Sri.S.B.Hangraki, learned counsel for the petitioners and Smt.Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance Company and perused the records.
5. It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that voluminous evidence has been placed before the Tribunal in the form of PWs-1 to 4 and Exs.P1 to P15 in proof of the accident.
There is no discussion or any reason assigned as to why the evidence so placed by the petitioners is not accepted.
The Tribunal while dismissing the claim petition has wrongly relied on the judgment in M.F.A.No.200493/2014.
In that case, there was no proper evidence establishing the accident.
Here, in this case, though the petitioners have proved the accident by sufficient evidence, the findings recorded in M.F.A.No.200493/2014 is not applicable to this case.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company contended that the petitioners, except adding three more witnesses, have not produced any iota of evidence in establishing the accident in question.

It is also submitted that this Court has already discussed the manner in which the accident had occurred, the evidence placed, so also the manner in which the claim has been preferred in connivance with the Police, recorded a clear finding that there was no such accident and therefore,
the Tribunal is right in relying on the judgment of this Court and also in appreciating the evidence relied upon by the petitioners while dismissing the claim petition, which do not call for interference by this court.
7.
We have given our anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on both sides and also perused the impugned judgment.
8. There is no dispute as to the insurance coverage given to the Tata Sumo vehicle by the Insurance Company.
The only precise question is the genuineness of the accident as claimed by the petitioners.

9. As pleaded by the petitioners, the deceased was riding the motor cycle along with his friend Sathanna Sajjan, who is none other than the husband of one Savitri and father of Rayappa, who are the petitioners in M.V.C.No.199/2012 filed before the Senior Civil Judge and MACT., Jewargi.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The MACT, Jewargi, after considering the evidence allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation by its judgment dated 07.12.2013.

Same has been assailed by the Insurance Company Parwati And Ors vs Raj Ahmed Bhatliwale And Anr on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186652813/
3 before this court in M.F.A.No.200493/2014.

entities.text: Insurance Company Parwati And Ors vs Raj Ahmed Bhatliwale And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. The learned Single Judge of this court by order dated 10.11.2016 has discussed the identical facts pleaded and also the evidence relied upon by the petitioners in that case and held that the deceased died in an unfortunate accident, but said accident being converted into a profitable venture by his family members to secure compensation from the insurer of an unknown vehicle.

It was also observed that the Tribunal has not even bothered to look into the documents available on record and has not properly appreciated the evidence on record in respect of manner in which the complaint is lodged, subsequent charge sheet being filed clearly indicates callousness with which the learned Member of the MACT has conducted the proceedings resulting in award of compensation.

11. We have noted that at para-9, it has been specifically observed that there were three riders in the motor cycle in excess of seating capacity of two and there is a possible threat for their own lives to ride the motor cycle with two pillions, which is not convenient and congenial to ride the motor cycle and there is a possibility of rider loosing control and causing the accident may be resulting in serious injury or death cannot be ruled out.
The learned Single Judge has also observed that the surviving person Sathanna Sajjan among three riders was alive, who has not been examined before the Tribunal.
It is specifically observed that the rider of the motor cycle Basavaraj Kesaratagi is the first tortfeasor and the pillion riders are the other tortfeasor in causing the accident.

The petitioners have failed to furnish the particulars of the vehicle which caused the accident and came to the conclusion that the involvement of the vehicle in question has not been established and consequently allowed the appeal and dismissed the claim petition in M.V.C.No.199/2012 by setting aside the judgment and award passed on 7.12.2013.
12.
Now, here, in this case, the second pillion rider has been brought before the Tribunal as PW- 4/Sangappa.
We have perused his evidence, which is made available in the T.C.R.

He asserted that while he was going towards Gulbarga along with Sathanna and Basavaraj in the motor cycle, near Nelogi Cross, a Tata Sumo came from the opposite direction and dashed against the motor cycle.
In the cross-examination, it is brought out from him that he was not aware of the registration number of the motor cycle and who is the owner of the said motor cycle.
Even he is unable to state the registration number of the Tata Sumo.
Though he has given Exs.P14 and P15/statements before the Police, he is unable to state what he has stated to them.
He was not aware in what speed the motor cycle was going.
From such a bald statement of this witness, nothing could be demonstrated as to how Tata Sumo came from the opposite direction, how the motor cycle being ridden.
13. Interestingly, the deceased pillion rider Sathanna Sajjan was his own son-in-law and deceased Basavaraj was his friend.
By examining the surviving pillion rider, nothing more is added to the evidence relied by the petitioners in M.V.C.No.199/2012.
In this background, we are not persuaded to accept the contentions raised by the petitioners in this case.
14. The petitioners in M.V.C.No.199/2012 have not challenged the findings of this court and thereby it has attained the finality.
As observed in the said judgment, examination of the surviving pillion rider will not add anything more.
Hence, we are of the considered view that the finding recorded by this court is binding on the petitioners.

Even otherwise, if the evidence on record is appreciated Parwati And Ors vs Raj Ahmed Bhatliwale And Anr on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186652813/
4

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: excluding the finding recorded by this court, nothing stands in support of the petitioners, which will establish the alleged accident and thereby giving a right to the petitioners to claim the compensation.

15. On a scrutiny of the impugned judgment with reference to the evidence relied upon by the parties, we are convinced that the alleged accident is make- believe, there is no proof of it and thereby the Tribunal has rightly assigned reasons in arriving at a conclusion that the petitioners have not established the accident to award compensation as claimed by them.
Hence, the appeal is devoid of merits and is liable to be dismissed.
16. In the result, we pass the following;
ORDER The appeal is dismissed.
